classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. Four finite first-coordinate choices and three second-coordinate choices give twelve pairs.

content.prompt:
Let $A$ and $B$ be two sets. The $\mathit{Cartesian\ product}$ of $A$ and $B$ is the set of all ordered pairs from $A$ and $B$.
$$A\times B=\{(a,b)\text{ where }a\in A,\ b\in B\}.$$
List the elements of, or describe geometrically, $A\times B$ for the following sets.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\{1,3,5,7\}\\B&=\{2,4,6\}\end{aligned}$$

answer.short:
$$\begin{aligned}A\times B=\{&(1,2),(1,4),(1,6),\\&(3,2),(3,4),(3,6),\\&(5,2),(5,4),(5,6),\\&(7,2),(7,4),(7,6)\}.\end{aligned}$$

Pair each of the four first coordinates with all three second coordinates.
